comparator.name: Health and Life Sciences
comparator.sourceNotes: For Fall 2026 entrants, the adopted 2026–2027 regulations establish ten compulsory 6 EC first-year courses and at least 30 EC open study in the first semester of Year 3. The curriculum revision removes the old BMW/DGZ/KW specialisations. Its Year 2 has six compulsory courses and four choice slots, including Genomics versus Qualitative Research and Anatomy/Physiology 2 versus System Transformation. It describes biomedical or societal research in Year 3, preparatory methods for the societal project and a final Science Communication course, but supplies no applicable future component-credit table. Old 18/24 EC thesis weights and outgoing specialisation tables cannot be imported. Lab safety is required before the Biochemistry practical; its grade also requires the Dutch diagnostic pass or completed refresher. Toxicology/Epidemiology requires completion of Year-1 study/career guidance. These noncredit conditions are separate from 180 EC. BSA normally requires 42 first-year EC. Attendance rules follow course manuals. Open study needs approval except stated minor exemptions, nonoverlap, at least 12 EC level 300 and at most 6 EC level 100; subjects in the degree field must be level 300. Listed minors remain conditional on entrance requirements and nonoverlap. Optional honours are excluded.
components: The lab safety course is required before the practical. The Biochemistry grade is recorded after the Dutch language test is passed or the refresher course is completed.
The grade is recorded after the first-year study and career guidance requirements are met.
At least 30 EC in the first semester of year three. Approval and course-level rules apply to individually chosen electives.

audience.programmeDescription: VU Health and Life Sciences examines health from cells and the human body to behavior, society, healthcare systems and the environment. Students starting in September 2026 combine biomedical and societal study in a revised curriculum.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The table shows the confirmed 60 EC first year and 30 EC of elective study in year three. The remaining credits and progression rules for the revised curriculum are still under review.

curriculum.limitation: This partial curriculum covers 90 of 180 EC for September 2026 entrants. The full credit and choice rules for year two and the credits and entry requirements for the final research and science communication courses still need confirmation.
